scope: Bounded camera alignment at the recursive H3 continuation seam
summary: A decaying Euclidean camera alignment slightly improved the rinse seam but moved the unscrew robot geometry and raised its full-frame seam MAD, so the aligned variant was rejected from delivery.
evidence: The unscrew ECC transform used 24 frames, correlation 0.5813, about 7.25 degrees rotation, and translations of 35.73/-63.21 pixels.
Unscrew seam MAD increased from 41.5532 without alignment to 43.5635 with alignment, and the review storyboard showed a larger robot-position jump.
The rinse seam improved from 16.8531 to 15.8029 MAD, but the task-level release unit is shared and the unscrew regression blocks promotion.
lessons: Background camera alignment cannot be promoted when it improves the scene but displaces the manipulated robot/object geometry.
Prefer the unblended state-valid seam when subject geometry is more important than a small background registration gain.
limitations: The alignment was a 2D camera-frame Euclidean warp, not calibrated 3D camera compensation.
next_actions: Retain the unaligned, task-state-valid recursive continuation for the published comparison.
